obligations.note: Change names ticket CHG-26613, a standard ticket approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-24, before review. Its components (payments.payments, payments.tests) cover every touched path: memos.py and payments.py map to payments.payments, and the new test file maps to payments.tests.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa@fernbrook.example, a change_approver for payments. She is a different person from the author, Jonah Weiss, under every address in the directory.
The approval names the head commit ded953b1aeb0, so it covers exactly what would be merged.

run.json shows the CI run was on the earlier commit be1f9edc, not the head. The later commit adds a new module constant (PREVIEW_MIN_WIDTH = 8) to memos.py, which is not a comment, whitespace or formatting edit, so that run does not count. The attached JUnit report is also suspect: it is timestamped 2026-10-23 from a personal machine (dev-laptop-7.local), which predates the commit and does not match executor ci-runner-04.

Ledger evidence covering payments.py (required_approvals for PAY-1, release for PAY-2) concerns symbols this change does not modify. The new approvals_remaining function is additive, so no accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change adds a display helper approvals_remaining and a memo constant, and has an approved ticket and an independent code review on the head commit. However, there is no valid test run on the final commit. CI ran on the first commit, and the follow-up commit is a code change, not comment-only or formatting. The JUnit report attached to the run also has inconsistent provenance: it was produced on a personal machine three days before the commit existed. CHG-4 is therefore violated and the change is rejected until the full suite is run in CI on ded953b1.
